neighbours.label: reading meaning into or projecting onto something ('read too much into', 'project onto')
fire: Critics tend to read too much into the director's choice of colours.
Try not to read anything into a single late reply.
Fans projected their own hopes onto the young candidate.
He kept reading hidden messages into her ordinary emails.
Children often project their feelings onto their toys.
Investors read a lot into the chairman's brief remarks.
We project our own motives onto people we barely know.
It is easy to read sinister intent into a simple mistake.
quiet: Critics tend to write long reviews of the director's films.
Try to send a quick reply to every email you get.
Fans waved flags as the young candidate arrived.
He kept filing her ordinary emails into one folder.
Children often carry their toys into the garden.
Investors listened to the chairman's brief remarks.
We send our own staff to meet people from abroad.
It is easy to spill coffee into the keyboard by mistake.

notes: Top examples: 'read (too much) into', 'project these notions', imagination. Probe: 'read too much into' 0.69, 'project fears onto' 1.0, literal 'walked into' 0.01.
